title: Latency-tiered shedding credit allocation and failover decision matrix
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define and implement a credit-based degradation allocation and a deterministic failover decision matrix for latency-sensitive model routes. This ticket produces the canonical SLI/SLO definitions, the error-budget draining/crediting algorithm, and the operational rules for regional failover and circuit-breaking behavior.
background: We currently handle overloads with coarse queue timeouts and global circuit breakers which result in large availability cliffs for latency-sensitive routes (chat-streaming, short-completion transactions). Customer teams requested smoother, predictable degradation and clearer signals when traffic will be degraded or failed over to other regions or cheaper variants.
motivation: Provide a predictable degradation path that: 1) limits user-visible disruption by preferring graceful quality/latency reduction over full failure; 2) makes error-budget accounting explicit and auditable at route+model granularity; 3) enables automated, reversible multi-region failover decisions.
proposal_summary: Introduce 'degradation credits' allocated per route variant that are consumed when requests exceed latency or correctness targets. Credits replenish slowly during healthy periods. Define a deterministic failover decision matrix that escalates from local shedding to partial regional fallback to full regional ejection. Couple burn-rate detectors to circuit breakers with hysteresis to avoid thrashing.
sli_definitions: latency-success-rate: fraction of requests that return within 300ms (p95 target window) and with 200 HTTP status, measured per route+model in 1m windows
streaming-liveness: fraction of active streaming sessions that produce at least one token within 150ms of client activity (measured per session over 30s windows)
quality-pass-rate: fraction of sampled responses that pass the route-specific promptset acceptance test (automated eval harness), sampled at 500 requests/hour per route and aggregated hourly
availability: fraction of requests that receive a non-5xx response within the route SLA latency (combined metric of success and latency)
error-budget-burn-rate: tokens consumed vs credits allocated in rolling 1h and 24h windows
slo_targets: quality-slo: quality-pass-rate >= 98% sampled hourly for production promptsets
degradation_credit_algorithm: initial_allocation: each route+model receives a baseline credit_wallet sized by expected qps: baseline_credits = max(1000, int(traffic_qps * 10))
consumption: when request exceeds latency target or returns at-risk quality, consume credit = 1 + latency_penalty_ms / 100 rounded up
tiered-penalties: for streaming routes, missing first-token deadlines consumes 3x credits during peak windows

replenishment: credits +=(baseline_credits * 0.01) per 5m if route is healthy (no p95 breaches in window) and +(baseline_credits * 0.05) on sustained quiet periods (>30m below 30% baseline load), capped at 2x baseline
credit-trading: tenant-aware reserved capacity may borrow credits from global pool under supervision; borrowing creates audit logs and reduces future replenish rate
credit-exhaustion: when credits drop below 10% baseline, route enters preemptive-shedding; when zero, route will be eligible for failover or variant downgrade
error_budget_handling: error_budget_accounting: maintain per-route+model hourly and 24h ledgers of credit balance and burn events
automated-mitigation: predefined mitigation actions mapped to credit thresholds (see failover_decision_matrix) are triggered by ledger state with automated runbook steps
manual-override: SREs can pause automated mitigation for 15m windows with annotated justification; overrides are logged and incrementally ratelimited
recovery-and-repurchase: when region returns to healthy, reclaimed credits are reconciled and a recovery bonus of 5% baseline credits is applied once per 24h to accelerate repair
failover_decision_matrix: state-0 (healthy): credits > 50% baseline => no shedding, normal routing

state-1 (soft degradation): credits between 10% and 50% => enable latency-tiered shedding rules: reduce non-critical features (N-best, re-ranking, chorus), degrade sampling temperature to preserve response time

state-2 (partial fallback): credits between 1% and 10% => route eligible for partial fallback: route-level traffic split to cheaper compatible variant (e.g., quantized variant) up to 30% traffic or to adjacent region with <200ms RTT for the client cohort

state-3 (regional ejection): credits == 0 or sustained burn-rate > 5x baseline for 15m => eject region for this route+model: traffic rerouted per regional-priority table and circuit breakers are engaged
decision-factors: current credits, burn-rate trend (1m/5m/15m), blacklist of incompatible variants, client-region latency constraints, customer tier (enterprise/premium may pin)
circuit_breaker_spec: transient-trigger: p95 latency breach > 5x SLO or instant 5xx rate > 2% in 1m window => open for 30s, probe after 30s with 5% traffic
persistent-trigger: sustained burn-rate > configured multiplier (default 3x) over 15m and credits at 0 => open for 5m and shift traffic per failover matrix
hysteresis: when closing, require 2 consecutive recovery windows with p95 < SLO and credits > 20% baseline
probe-strategy: slow probes with canary traffic plus shadow comparisons for quality SLI; failing probes extend open state exponentially up to 1h
metrics-to-evaluate-before-open: combined score of latency z-score, 5xx rate, quality-pass-rate drop; multi-factor threshold reduces false positives
rollout_plan: phase-1: specification and implement ledger + credit accounting (2 sprints) - unit tests and simulation harness
phase-2: implement local shedding rules and credit-based throttles behind feature flag (1 sprint) - dogfood on internal routes
phase-3: integrate failover decision matrix and circuit breaker hooks; staged rollout to canary tenants (2 weeks)
phase-4: enable automated mitigation with runbook links; observe burn behavior for 4 weeks; iterate thresholds
phase-5: document ops runbooks and add to Console: per-route credit dashboard, drilldowns, and audit trail
monitoring_and_alerting: dashboards: per-route credit balances, burn-rate heatmap, failover state timeline, probe success rate
alerts: 1) credit < 25% baseline (P3), 2) credit < 10% baseline (P2), 3) credit == 0 or sustained burn 3x baseline (P1), 4) probe failure after circuit-breaker open (P0)
runbooks: link triggered alerts to playbook steps (investigate model variant health, check kernel-fallbacks, review recent deploys)
analysis: automated hourly report of top 10 routes by credit consumption and top 5 drivers (latency, 5xx, quality)
testing_and_validation: unit-tests: credit accounting invariants, replenish math, edge cases for negative balances
simulations: synthetic traffic generator that exercises spike shapes (saw, burst, steady) to validate failover thresholds and hysteresis
chaos-tests: induce regional NIC flaps and kernel timeouts in staging to validate automated ejection and recovery flows
evals: quality-pass-rate probes using golden promptsets run during canary and probe phases
open_questions: 1) Should enterprise tenants be allowed to opt out of automated ejection entirely, or only above a pinned traffic percentage?
2) How do we factor model-cost delta when choosing fallback variant vs cross-region routing (cost-aware routing)?
3) What SLA communications should be emitted to customers during preemptive-shedding vs regional ejection?
4) Should quality-pass-rate sampling be mandatory for all routes or configurable per project?
